value: After the 1849 Montreal fire destroyed the Parliament buildings and their library, the Ottawa library was insisted upon as a separate structure with fire-proof iron doors.
quote: insisting that the new library be housed in a separate structure with fire-proof iron doors

value: Architects in the 1859 competition for the Parliament buildings had just ten weeks to meet detailed requirements, according to Hill Notes.
quote: given just ten weeks to meet detailed requirements

value: In the 1952 fire, firefighters used nearly 910,000 litres of water and about 150,000 volumes had to be taken off the shelves.
quote: nearly 910,000 litres of water

value: A painting of the Virgen de Trapani hangs at the far end of the hall, framed by gilded neoclassical columns.
quote: una pintura de la Virgen de Trapani espera al fondo

value: Bishop Palafox never saw the project finished. The Associated Press says the library he founded in 1646 is the first public library in the Americas.
quote: no vio su proyecto terminado

value: The Palafoxiana holds 45,000 items on more than 15,000 subjects, dated from the 17th to the 20th century, according to the Mexican culture ministry in 2019.
quote: alberga 45 mil ejemplares

value: The books sit on cedar shelves in three levels, arranged by a scholastic view that places God as the base of all knowledge. The first level holds more than 11,000 Bibles and religious works, according to the Associated Press.
quote: estantes de cedro que se distribuyen en tres niveles

value: The Baltimore Sun reported in 2016 that the library's books were getting their first proper cleaning in 50 to 60 years.
quote: proper cleaning in 50 to 60 years

value: The original glass skylight was at some point replaced with plastic panels, which later failed.
quote: original glass skylight had been replaced at some point with plastic

value: The original iron trusses above the atrium were made at the Phoenix Iron Works, while Bartlett-Robbins and Company fabricated the neo-classical cast-iron designs.
quote: original iron trusses were made at the Phoenix Iron Works

value: The skylight measures 25 by 75 feet, a total of 1,875 square feet.
quote: 25 x 75 feet for a total of 1,875 square feet

value: An ancient report says Ptolemy imprisoned the Alexandrian scholar Aristophanes of Byzantium on suspicion of leaving for Pergamon.
quote: is said to have imprisoned Aristophanes of Byzantium

value: Crates of Mallus, a scholar from Pergamon, fell into a Roman sewer opening around 169 BC while on an embassy. He broke his leg.
quote: as an envoy to the Senate in about 169 BC, he fell into a sewer opening and broke his leg

value: Pliny reports a story that Ptolemy banned papyrus exports and that parchment (charta pergamena) was invented at Pergamon as a substitute. The same page notes Herodotus says animal skins were used for writing long before.
quote: parchment ( charta pergamena ) was said to have been invented in Pergamon as a substitute

value: Strabo writes that the heirs of Neleus, who held the books of Aristotle and Theophrastus, hid them in a trench to keep them from the Attalid book-hunters. Moisture and moths damaged them.
quote: in a kind of trench. But much later, when the books had been damaged by moisture and moths

value: The rooms on the Athena terrace long taken for the royal library may not have been one. Later scholars have suggested a reception hall, a store for offerings or a display room.
quote: It therefore is not certain that the rooms originally thought to have been the location of the Pergamon Library actually served that purpose

value: During the restoration that ran to the end of 2022 the books were covered, then taken from the shelves one by one and cleaned once the work was finished.
quote: were professionally covered during the restoration and were removed from the shelves one by one and cleaned after the work was completed

value: Prince Eugene of Savoy's library of 15,000 volumes stands in the middle oval, bound in red, blue and yellow Morocco leather.
quote: the library of Prince Eugene in the middle oval, containing 15,000 volumes bound in red, blue and yellow Morocco leather

value: The hall holds 128 bookcases and shelves, 48 windows, 20 doors, 17 statues and 12 busts.
quote: 128 bookcases and shelves 48 windows 20 doors and 28 tables/display cabinets 17 statues and 12 busts

value: The marble statue of Emperor Charles VI at the centre shows him as Hercules Musarum. It dates from 1735 and was allegedly made by court sculptor Antonio Corradini.
quote: It dates back to 1735 and was allegedly crafted by Imperial Court sculptor Antonio Corradini

value: A white stone head of David Sassoon sits above the entrance portico.
quote: Above the entrance portico is a white stone head of David Sassoon.

value: The idea for the library came from twelve mechanics working at the Bombay Mint.
quote: The idea of the library was mooted by twelve mechanics employed in the Bombay Mint.

value: The story goes that David Sassoon nailed a mezuzah to his doorpost at 9 Tamarind Lane when he settled in Bombay.
quote: nailed his mezuza, the sign of a Jewish home, to his doorpost at 9 Tamarind Lane

value: An hour after Ned Kelly's death in 1880, his hair and beard were shaved and plaster was applied to his face and head to make a death mask.
quote: An hour after his death, his hair and beard were shaved, and plaster was applied to his face and head to make a death mask.

value: In 1965 the armour was taken off public view and moved to the care of the State Library.
quote: in 1965 the armour was taken off view and transferred to the care of the Library

value: Ned Kelly's armour is made from farm machinery. The Library says historians have guessed the parts were stolen or gifted and forged by sympathetic blacksmiths, but none of that is confirmed.
quote: The armour is constructed from farm machinery. Historians have speculated that the parts may have been stolen or gifted

value: The Burke and Wills expedition papers were deposited in the Melbourne Public Library in March 1875.
quote: deposited in the Melbourne Public Library in March 1875

value: The Jerilderie Letter was written out by Joe Byrne at Ned Kelly's dictation over a few months. Kelly meant it to be printed in the press.
quote: dictated by Ned Kelly to fellow Kelly gang member Joe Byrne. It was written over a period of a few months

value: The Guénebault collection holds about 28,000 prints from the 17th to the 19th century.
quote: Collection Guénebault Collection d’environ 28 000 estampes du 17 e au 19 e s.

value: The library keeps scientific instruments, ethnographic objects and works of art from the old Sainte-Geneviève abbey, including pieces from its cabinet of curiosities.
quote: une collection d’instruments scientifiques, d’objets ethnographiques et d’œuvres d’art provenant de l’abbaye Sainte-Geneviève, notamment de son cabinet de curiosités

value: The reserve holds a Henri Labrouste collection of the drawings and texts behind the building of the library, dated 1843 to 1850.
quote: Fonds Henri Labrouste Sources graphiques et textuelles de la construction de la bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève (1843-1850)

value: From the 10th to the 16th century the books were kept in the Hartmut Tower, which came through several fires that raged through the abbey and the town.
quote: tucked safely away in the Hartmut Tower, it defied many threats and several fires that raged through the abbey and the town

value: The abbey's oldest library catalogue, Cod. Sang. 728, dates from about 860 to 870 and is still kept in the library.
quote: The oldest library catalogue in St.Gallen, c. 860/870 (St.Gallen, Abbey Library, Cod. Sang. 728, p. 12)

value: The library holds an Egyptian mummy, Shepenese, dated to the 7th century BC. It reached the library only after the abbey was dissolved.
quote: One item that was not originally in the cabinet of curiosities is the Egyptian mummy Shepenese (7th c. BC).

value: A stucco border around the exterior carries 294 hieroglyph-like images of the subjects found inside.
quote: hieroglyphic-like motifs of all the subjects to be found within (294 images)

value: Asplund took the pattern of the rotunda floor from the marble floor of the Pantheon in Rome.
quote: Asplund based the pattern on the marble floor on that in the Pantheon in Rome

value: In Nils Dardel's fresco The Sandman, the old man with the rifle is supposed to be the painter's father-in-law, Axel Klinckowström.
quote: The old man on the left with a rifle in his hand is supposed to be Dardel’s father-in-law, a man by the name of Axel Klinckowström

value: Some of the windows in room 2 are blind, made of painted iron and polished plate glass, and reflect light to make the room look wider.
quote: blind windows of painted iron and polished plate glass that on first glance give the impression of real windows

value: The children's library ceiling shows the night sky at 8 pm on 22 September, Asplund's birthday.
quote: The ceiling painting in the first room shows the starry sky at 8 pm at the autumnal equinox on 22 September (Gunnar Asplund’s birthday)

value: The first gallery of the rotunda opened to visitors only in 1974. Until then only librarians went up.
quote: Gallery 1 was first opened to visitors in 1974 and the stairs up to it were built at the same time and designed by Gunnar Asplund’s son, Hans Asplund. Until then, only librarians

value: A star atlas made in Venice in the mid-14th century is among the library's illuminated manuscripts. It was probably in the library of Charles IV.
quote: star atlas from Venice, written and decorated in the mid-14th century (exhibited in the globe collection exhibition). It was likely in the library of Charles IV.

value: After 1950, when Czechoslovakia abolished religious orders, the Strahov Library was incorporated into the newly established National Literature Memorial.
quote: the Strahov Library was incorporated into the newly established National Literature Memorial

value: The Theological Hall holds a so-called compilation wheel, a device made for more comfortable study.
quote: In the Theological Hall, you can see a device for more comfortable study, the so-called compilation wheel.

value: The oldest manuscript in the library is a gospel book, probably written around 860 in Tours. Four full-page illuminations of the evangelists were added at Trier in the tenth century.
quote: The oldest manuscript kept in the Strahov Library contains, as its name suggests, all four gospels. The text was probably written around 860 in Tours (France)

value: After the last Maratha queen died, the palace property and library were tied up in the civil courts. Royal family members removed the library from the suit and endowed it to the public with one lakh rupees.
quote: dedicated this Library to the public with one lakh

value: Ink for the manuscripts was made from sesame-oil lamp soot, acacia gum and rainwater. Paper was dipped in turmeric water to keep insects off.
quote: The papers were dipped in turmeric water for protection from insects

value: On his pilgrimage to Banares, Serfoji II employed many pandits to collect, buy and copy a vast number of works. The library carries his name.
quote: employed many Pandits to collect, buy and copy a vast number of works

value: The Sarasvati Mahal holds a grammar of the rare dialect Bhandira-bhasha among works the library says are unique to it.
quote: the grammar of the rare dialect called Bhandira-bhasha

value: Fan Qin's rules for the library included a ban on entering it after drinking alcohol.
quote: Fan set up strict rules to manage his library, including one that forbade people from going there after drinking alcohol

value: In 1585, aged 80, Fan Qin split his property into savings and the library of 70,000 books and let his descendants choose. The one who took the library became its keeper.
quote: He asked his descendants to choose

value: A rescue worker told HMML she showed photos of the 1,400 metal boxes used to carry Timbuktu manuscripts out.
quote: She showed me photos of the 1,400 metal boxes

value: HMML counts more than 200,000 manuscripts from some 36 libraries in Timbuktu. Other figures on this site run higher, so treat the number as approximate.
quote: more than 200,000 from some 36 libraries

value: Libraries that stayed in Timbuktu were hidden by their owners, as families had done when the Moroccans invaded in the late sixteenth century and the French in the nineteenth.
quote: hidden by their owners in the same manner as when the Moroccans invaded in the late sixteenth century

value: The Mamma Haidara Family Library is one of the largest private manuscript collections in Timbuktu. Some of its documents date to the 13th century.
quote: has one of the largest private manuscript collections in Timbuktu, and some of its documents date back to the 13th century

value: In 2006 Gabriel Orozco installed an 11.7 metre grey whale skeleton in the library. It was found beached on Isla Arena in Baja California.
quote: installed an 11.7 metre grey whale skeleton in Mexico City

value: The book stacks are painted military green and hang from steel girders above the main hall.
quote: The book stacks, painted military green, are suspended above the hall by steel girders

value: The botanical garden covers 70 per cent of the site and holds almost 60,000 plants of 168 species, according to El Universal.
quote: 168 especies de árboles, arbustos y hierbas

value: The library closed in March 2007 with more than 3,000 unfinished tasks. Critics said the Fox government had rushed construction to open before a hotly contested election.
quote: list of more than 3,000 unfinished tasks

value: The reassembled whale skeleton consists of 169 bones, with only one of the tympanums missing.
quote: consisted of 169 bones

value: In 1902 the library bought its old seventeenth-century rival, the Barberini Library, together with the baroque shelving that held it.
quote: purchased the Barberini Library, which had rivalled it in importance in the seventeenth century, along with the Barberini Archives and the baroque wooden shelving

value: In 1927 Pius XI turned the old stables in the Belvedere courtyard, made redundant by the motor car, into stacks for printed books.
quote: rendered the old stables in the Cortile del Belvedere (to one’s right when facing the entrance to the Library), Pope Pius XI (1922-1939) decided to transform them into stacks

value: Part of the medieval papal library, left at Avignon, passed to the Borghese family in the 1600s and was bought by Leo XIII in 1891.
quote: what remained in Avignon at the beginning of the seventeenth century came into the collection of the Borghese family, purchased in 1891 by Leo XIII

value: Readers could borrow books from the early library, and the loan registers for 1475 to 1547 survive.
quote: the records of the books loaned during the years 1475-1547 are still in existence

value: The French occupations of Rome in 1798-99 and 1809 cost the library nearly all of its coin and medal collection.
quote: led to considerable losses, including that of nearly all the numismatic collection which had been gathered up until then

value: Atisha is sometimes listed as a notable abbot of Vikramashila.
quote: is sometimes listed as a notable abbot

value: Excavators found brick-arched underground chambers beneath some monk cells. The Survey thinks they were probably for confined meditation.
quote: probably meant for confined meditation by the monks

value: The Archaeological Survey of India says the library building was cooled by water from the adjoining reservoir, run through vents in its back wall. It suggests this was meant to protect fragile manuscripts.
quote: It was air-conditioned by cooled water of the adjoining reservoir through a range of vents in the back wall.

value: The Bihar tourism corporation says Dharmapala founded Vikramashila in response to a supposed decline in scholarship at Nalanda.
quote: in response to a supposed decline in the quality of scholarship at Nalanda

value: The Survey puts the university at more than a hundred teachers and about a thousand students.
quote: more than hundred teachers and about one thousand students

value: Vikramashila is known mainly from Tibetan sources, above all the writings of the monk historian Taranatha, not from Indian chronicles.
quote: It is known to us mainly through Tibetan sources specially the writings of Taranath

value: About 25,000 badly burnt book blocks, plus many fragments, called ash books, were recovered from the rubble. Since 2008 some have been restored by a mass process the library calls unique worldwide.
quote: die sogenannten Aschebücher. Ein Teil von ihnen wird seit 2008 in einem weltweit einzigartigen Mengenverfahren restauriert

value: After the 2004 fire, single leaves carried by the wind into the streets and gardens of Weimar were still being handed to the library months later.
quote: Einzelne Blätter, die der Wind in die Straßen und Gärten Weimars getragen hatte, wurden der Bibliothek noch Monate nach dem Brand übergeben

value: The Book Tower's top gallery holds the Weimar military library, described as the most completely preserved German military library of around 1800.
quote: Sie ist heute die am vollständigsten erhaltene Militärbibliothek Deutschlands der Zeit um 1800

value: The spiral staircase in the Book Tower has a spindle made from a single oak trunk twelve metres high, which came from the Osterburg in Weida.
quote: Die Spindel der Treppe ist aus einem einzigen, zwölf Meter hohen Eichenstamm gefertigt und stammt ursprünglich aus der Osterburg in Weida.

value: After secularisation the monastery briefly became a ducal residence, then served as an infantry barracks known as the Schlosskaserne.
quote: Dann machte Herzog Heinrich von Württemberg Wiblingen für kurze Zeit zum Schloss. Später wurde Wiblingen dauerhaft als Infanteriekaserne genutzt

value: At the centre of the 1744 ceiling fresco is a woman ringed by angels, who stands for divine wisdom ruling over all.
quote: Im Mittelpunkt des Gemäldes steht eine von Engeln umgebene Frauengestalt: die göttliche Weisheit, die über allem herrscht.

value: The monastery's own account says the ghost of Father Johannes, a forgetful 18th-century priest, comes to the library hall every night to look for a book holding his confession notes. It presents this as a legend.
quote: Seitdem, so erzählt man sich, muss Pater Johannes jede Nacht in den Bibliothekssaal kommen, um nach dem Buch mit dem Notizzettel zu suchen
